title: Hereditary Fructose Intolerance
authors: Gaughan S, Ayres L, Baker PR II
result: Initial posting 17 December 2015; last update 18 February 2021. Autosomal recessive; biallelic pathogenic ALDOB variants. Prevalence estimated from carrier testing: 1 in 18,000 (United Kingdom), 1 in 26,000 (Germany), 1 in 31,000 (Poland), 1 in 60,000 (United States). p.Ala150Pro (legacy Ala149Pro) is the most common variant in all studies. Accumulated fructose 1-phosphate inhibits gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis, causes overuse and reduced regeneration of ATP, and impairs protein glycosylation. After fructose, sucrose or sorbitol, untreated patients develop hypoglycaemia, vomiting and metabolic disturbances, and may progress to hepatic and renal failure; with early dietary restriction of fructose, sucrose, sorbitol and sucralose, quality of life and life expectancy are normal.
